title: Uhud: those who shielded him
hookLine: Nusaybah bint Ka'b, Talhah and Abu Talhah shield the wounded Prophet ﷺ with their bodies, and Fatimah tends his wound (sirah; Bukhari)

cards: Same battle, a little later. The hill is empty, the enemy has come around it, and the Muslim lines have broken. People are running.
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is hurt, and a rumor goes through the field that he has been killed. Around him, a handful of people do the opposite of running. They close in.
One of them came out that morning carrying nothing but a water skin. Her name was Nusaybah bint Ka'b, and she is remembered as Umm Umarah. Today: Uhud, and the ones who stood in front.

teach.h: A WATER SKIN, THEN A SWORD AND A BOW.
teach.b: Nusaybah's story comes through the early biographers, in Ibn Ishaq's account. Later, another woman asked her about Uhud, and she told it plainly. She had gone out early with a water skin, to give the fighters a drink.
When the Muslims were routed, she went to where the Prophet was and fought, with a sword and with a bow, to keep people away from him, until she was wounded herself.
The woman who asked saw the scar on her shoulder, deep and hollow. Nusaybah was not the only one. Sahih al-Bukhari keeps two more.
A man named Qays saw the hand of Talhah ibn Ubaydullah, paralyzed: the hand he had held up to shield the Prophet at Uhud.
And Anas says that Abu Talhah, a strong archer, stood before the Prophet with his shield, and when the Prophet raised his head to look at the enemy, told him: don't look out, an arrow might hit you.
My chest before your chest. Then what came after. Bukhari reports that the Prophet's face was cut, his helmet broken on his head, a tooth broken.
Fatimah, the bride from two days ago, washed the blood from his face while Ali poured water from his shield.
When the bleeding wouldn't stop, she burned a piece of a reed mat and pressed the ash into the wound, and it stopped. A water skin, a raised hand, a shield, a handful of ash.
Each of them stood between him and harm.

how: Muslims retell the defenders of Uhud in sirah lessons and sermons, and Nusaybah bint Ka'b, Umm Umarah, is named as an example of women's courage in the early community.

o: a truce made with the Meccans after one day
a raid on a Meccan caravan along the coast
the battle where a few shielded the wounded Prophet

p: came out with water, then fought
a hand paralyzed shielding the Prophet

s: Nusaybah went out to Uhud to fight
in her own telling, she went out with a water skin to give the fighters a drink, and fought only when the lines broke.
Talhah's hand was paralyzed from shielding the Prophet ﷺ
Qays says in Bukhari that he saw it, the hand Talhah held up at Uhud.
the Prophet's bleeding was stopped with cold water
water didn't stop it; Fatimah burned a piece of a mat and pressed the ash into the wound.

games.q: you've come to the battle carrying a water skin for the fighters. the lines break and people are running past you. what do you do?
o: keep handing out water at the back.
go to where the Prophet ﷺ is.
games.why: in her own account, Nusaybah went to the Prophet and fought to keep people away from him, until she was wounded.

practice: Bring to mind one person taking blows right now, online, at work, in their family or in their own head, and picture yourself stepping a little closer, the way Nusaybah moved toward the Prophet instead of away.
Ask what your water skin is, your shield, your ash: a message, a word in a meeting, a meal at the door. If you pray, you can ask Allah to protect them; if not, just keep them in front of you.

wordCard.voice: Uhud, again: the battle where the lines broke, and Nusaybah, Talhah, Abu Talhah and Fatimah each stood between the Prophet and harm. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Nusaybah, the name of Umm Umarah, who shielded the Prophet ﷺ at Uhud.

carryVoice: Your line: she stood in front. Four people, four small things, all moving toward him. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (via Ibn Hisham): Umm Umarah, Nusaybah bint Ka'b, at Uhud, in her own telling
Sahih al-Bukhari 3724 (Qays: Talhah's hand, paralyzed from shielding the Prophet)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3811 (Anas: Abu Talhah with his shield; 'my chest before your chest')
Sahih al-Bukhari 2911 / 4075 (the Prophet's wounds; Fatimah washes them, Ali pours water, the ash of a burned mat)
